Description:
A hemisphere of D80 closed off by a D80 cylinder 100 long, built THREE ways that must all produce the same solid: the lower half of a sphere r=40 centred on the origin (z -40..0) plus a cylinder r=40 from z=0 to z=100.
  resA - union of the cylinder with the WHOLE sphere; the sphere's upper half is inside the cylinder
  resB - union of the cylinder with the lower half only, split off first, so the two meet in a coincident disc at z=0
  resC - one revolve of the meridian profile, no boolean involved
Sphere and cylinder have the same radius, so their surfaces touch tangentially along the circle z=0 - two tangential periodic surfaces. That contact used to break every operation between them; resA and resB are the guard against it coming back.
The rest of the case checks that the three results are interchangeable, which is the real claim: dAC and dCA compare resA against resC as point sets and must be empty, iAC and uAC combine them, and pAB does the same for the two boolean-built solids as a control. Three constructions of one solid should not behave differently in a later operation.
Expected:
All three are one closed, consistent solid with extent -40, -40, -40, 40, 40, 100 and the same volume:
  hemisphere  2/3*pi*40^3            = 134041.286553
  cylinder    pi*40^2*100            = 502654.824574
  total                              = 636696.111128
Surface area, exact: hemisphere 2*pi*40^2 = 10053.096491, cylinder wall 2*pi*40*100 = 25132.741229, top disc pi*40^2 = 5026.548246, total 40212.385966. There is no bottom face - the hemisphere closes it.
Because the three are the same point set, the combinations are forced:
  dAC = resA - resC   EMPTY, recorded as "exists": "false"
  dCA = resC - resA   EMPTY
  iAC = resA n resC   the whole solid, 636696.111128
  uAC = resA u resC   the whole solid, 636696.111128
  pAB = resA n resB   the whole solid, 636696.111128  (control: no revolve involved)
Note on the recorded numbers: the baseline volume comes from ShellMetrics with its own precision (size/1000, so 0.18 for this shell), not from the inspect.properties calls in RPCCalls, which ask for 1e-5. The two differ in the last digits; the inspect calls are there for stepping through with -r. iAC used to be left out of the closing inspect.summary because the name did not exist while the defect was open; it is back in since 2026-08-26.
Note on the FACE COUNTS: resA, resB, resC and pAB have 6 faces, but iAC has 8 and uAC has 7. That is not a defect. Combining two representations of the same point set splits faces along the boundaries the two shells happen to carry, and where those boundaries sit is free. What has to agree is the point set, and volume, area and extent say it does.
Status:
OK since 2026-08-26. All three constructions agree and all five combinations between them are right.

THREE DEFECTS, ALL CLOSED. The case was written while every one of them was open, which is why its
Description carries so much argument.

FIXED 2026-08-16 - tangential contact of periodic surfaces. The D80 sphere and the D80 coaxial cylinder
could not be combined at all: union returned the two operands unmerged, difference returned empty,
intersect dropped the tangentially touching component. resA and resB now agree with each other to 7e-11
and with the exact 636696.111128 to 6.8e-6.

FIXED 2026-08-16 - the revolve volume. solid.rotate on a profile containing a circular arc reported
535395.360 against the exact 636696.111, -15.9 percent, and tightening the precision made it WORSE
(532948.908 at 1e-8), so it converged to a wrong value rather than being a tessellation artefact. The
shape was right all along - dAC and dCA were empty then too. resC now measures -5.2e-6.

FIXED 2026-08-26 - a solid from solid.rotate is now interchangeable with the boolean-built one. The two
operations that contradicted the other three are right:
  resA n resC   was EMPTY, is 636695.177896   (-1.5e-6)
  resA u resC   was a 5-face fragment reaching only z -40..0, i.e. the hemisphere alone, and is now one
                solid over the full z -40..100 at 636693.417801   (-4.2e-6)
The old diagnosis pointed at resC having 6 faces and 10 EDGES where resA, resB and pAB have 6 and 12,
and that difference is still there - the revolve does lay out its seams differently. So the edge layout
was not the cause; whatever was, the classification now matches the two shells up regardless.

STILL OPEN, and deliberately NOT part of this case because an exception aborts the run before the
fingerprint is collected: the difference of two COINCIDENT solids throws instead of returning the empty
result. Re-checked on 2026-08-26, it still reproduces. Run this case, then
  {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":99,"method":"solid.boolean","params":{"op":"difference","a":"resA","b":"resB","name":"dAB","rebind":false}}
-> "The given key 'CADability.GeoObject.Face' was not present in the dictionary". resA and resB are the
same point set, so the answer should be empty. intersect and union on that same pair are fine, so it is
the difference specifically. Worth its own case file.

periodic surfaces that used to be one face are now split into two.
